Elham is now inside the main antagonist's domain and must find a way out without being discovered. The immediate pressure is identity concealment: humans are registered in this realm, and any slip could expose her as both a human and an Author — a status the higher-ups actively watch for. The Sparrow brought her there under the premise of taking her somewhere she could get something she needed, but Elham knows exactly who he is and who he serves, making acceptance of his offer its own kind of danger; refusal risked arousing suspicion from him or, worse, his leader. She suspects some of her fear is paranoia, yet she is correct to treat the threat as real — the main antagonist is not publicly irredeemable, which makes her privately held knowledge about him (including the softer side he has never willingly disclosed) particularly dangerous should he learn its source. The draft positions her as someone who must navigate that domain while keeping both her humanity and her authorial knowledge hidden.
